public.prompt: An editable Angular table receives a newly allocated array after each server refresh and can reorder its rows. Each record has a stable unique `id`; focused inputs and child state should follow the same record while DOM churn stays low. Which `@for` tracking expression fits?

options.label: Track `$index` so each rendered position keeps its existing row view after a reorder.
Track `record.id` so each logical record retains its row identity across arrays and reorders.
Track `record` so each freshly allocated object reference defines the next row identity.

answerProof.summary: A stable unique record ID gives Angular the same logical identity across new object instances and position changes, enabling row views to move with their records.
decisiveConstraints: The server refresh replaces object references.
Rows can move to different indices.
Each record exposes a stable unique identifier.

claims.statement: Angular's `@for` track expression associates data items with DOM nodes and should use a uniquely identifying property when one exists.
Tracking by object identity uses reference equality, which changes when refreshed records are newly allocated.

optionRationales.explanation: An index identifies a position, so a reorder can associate an existing row view and its local state with a different record.
optionRationales.plausibility: Index tracking can be efficient for collections whose membership and order remain static.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Records can move between positions while their state must follow the record.

optionRationales.explanation: The ID survives both object replacement and reordering, allowing Angular to retain the row view that belongs to each logical record.
Reference identity changes for every refreshed object, so Angular cannot match the new records to their previous row views.
optionRationales.plausibility: Object identity can work when the same instances remain in memory and only their order changes.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Every server refresh allocates replacement record objects.
